g.text: A bike the app cannot drive earns the Pro upgrade when its test passes in full
A FREE rider who runs the compatibility test on an unlisted trainer can earn a one-time Pro upgrade for the
scorecard. A bike the app can read but cannot drive earns it on the same terms: every row that applies to it passes.
Its control rows read N/A, because there is nothing to drive, and N/A counts as passed. Pairing, Indoor Bike Data
and Endurance must pass; any FAIL means no grant.
This reverses PHASE-021's first rule, which refused the grant to every such bike. Edwin failed this check on that
rule on 2026-09-13 ("these trainers are valid trainers, we should make it possible for these people to get a free
pro license if they validate their trainer fully") and confirmed the reversal on 2026-10-16.
TASK-1094-ADataOnlyTrainerThatPassesItsTestInFullEarnsTheProGrant built it.
Test the scorecard screen on Android, where the submission flow lives. The Pro-grant path is deliberately
Android-only (PARITYMATRIX B.7). Step 8 is the iOS half.
Setup
A FREE rider, because the grant copy only appears at FREE. Cheapest: Developer Options, "Tier Override (Debug)" set
to Free, then restart the app.
Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer",
then fully quit and reopen the app. Set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Refuses control — every target
write answered Control Not Permitted". It acts on writes, so it applies at once. Start and abandon a Power workout
first, so the three refusals latch the trainer data-only before the test runs.
On Android, do not use "Failure mode:" for this. That list only reaches the compatibility test's own mock (the "Run
this test against a mock trainer (no hardware; ~15 s, not remembered)" checkbox), not the fake trainer the rest of
the app connects to.
On iOS, turn on Use mock trainer in Settings → Developer · Trainer, set Mock trainer capability to Off and Mock
failure mode to Refuses control, then fully close and reopen the app. Connect the mock and start a Power workout
until repeated refusals latch data-only before running its compatibility test. This Mock failure mode drives the
whole-app iOS mock; it is separate from Android's compatibility-test-only "Failure mode:" control.
For step 7, the override set back to "Off — the trainer's real answer".
The iOS build on a second device, for step 8.
Steps
The scorecard
1. Settings, Equipment: run the compatibility test. Watch the progress bar.
